text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 streaming latency > 2.5s and multiple streaming stalls in eu-west1 (service: streaming-api) — 23% of requests showing tail stalls, SLO risk. Paging alice.
Alice (oncall): on it, paging infra and netops. grabbing logs now. @Ben @Eva can you ack?
Ben (infra): ack. seeing p95 increase too. pulling routing tables and NAT metrics.
Carmen (sre): I see correlated TLS handshake spikes from eu-west1 AZ-b to AZ-c at ~1880123300. Lots of retransmits on the egress path.
Diego (support): several customers reported degraded streaming sessions and partial transcripts cutting off. CS impact count ~12 active teams.
Alice (oncall): quick customer impact check — Diego can you list top affected customers and whether they hit errors vs slow tails?
Diego (support): mostly slow tails, a couple 499s when clients disconnected. customers: Acme, Nimbus Labs, Inboxly. Priority: Acme (PLG freemium -> paid conversion), Nimbus on enterprise trial.
Ben (infra): NAT gateway egress bandwidth looks normal but ephemeral port exhaustion spikes in AZ-b NAT metrics. Also seeing an increase in path MTU discovery drops on the cross-AZ NAT path.
Eva (netops): confirmed. TCP MSS clamping counters incrementing on the edge routers between AZ-b and AZ-c. Possibly packet fragmentation causing reordering and handshake jitter.
Carmen (sre): timeframe lines up with a rolling config push to the egress load-balancer in AZ-b at 1880123205. Could be an ACL or MTU mismatch introduced.
Alice (oncall): mitigation brainstorm: 1) failover traffic for streaming-api to AZ-d (same region) 2) revert egress LB config in AZ-b 3) enable MSS clamping on nat-gateway instances 4) temporarily route customer-critical traffic to dedicated NAT pool.
Ben (infra): I can flip route to AZ-d for the streaming-fleet behind the regional router — low risk, brief reconnections. prepping rollout. ETA 5m.
Eva (netops): MSS clamping patch ready to apply (iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) on the nat-gw autoscaling group. If we do that, it should avoid fragmentation-induced stalls. Will hold until we failover to avoid mixed-path oddities.
Carmen (sre): while Ben works failover I'll open tcpdump on a few affected hosts to capture retransmit patterns and TLS handshake timings.
Alice (oncall): good. Diego, please DM affected customers we have an incident and may cause brief reconnects during mitigation. status page update queued.
Diego (support): message sent to Acme & Nimbus. Posted status page with "degraded streaming performance in eu-west1; engineers investigating".
Ben (infra): starting route shift: moving 30% traffic to AZ-d (canary). command: `gcloud compute routers update --region=eu-west1 --set-traffic=streaming-api:30%:az-d` (internal shorthand). pushing now.
Incident Bot: Deployment event: routing-change triggered by Ben at 1880123502.
Carmen (sre): tcpdump snippet (example):
```
12:05:12.345678 IP 10.11.12.13.54321 > 54.23.12.1.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS,WS], length 0
12:05:12.456789 IP 54.23.12.1.443 > 10.11.12.13.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, options [mss 1400], length 0
12:05:12.457000 IP 10.11.12.13.54321 > 54.23.12.1.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0, length 0
```
Carmen (sre): note mss mismatch 1460 vs 1400 — indicates MTU/PMTU mismatch on return path, causing handshake resets and stalls.
Eva (netops): confirming upstream router announced smaller MTU to AZ-c path recently. I can temporarily enable MSS clamping on nat-gw group for AZ-b to AZ-c egress.
Alice (oncall): Ben, how's canary traffic looking? any change in p99 for the canary group?
Ben (infra): canary (30% AZ-d) shows p99 back to baseline ~400ms, full AZ-b group still elevated p99 ~2.8s. Good sign.
Diego (support): customers reported fewer stalls after the canary shift — Inboxly saw improvement.
Ben (infra): promoting to 60% to AZ-d for streaming-api. executing now.
Incident Bot: Route-change event: streaming-api traffic 60% AZ-d at 1880123575.
Carmen (sre): triggering MSS clamp on AZ-b NAT pool now to avoid mixed MTU behaviour for remaining sessions. command: `for i in $(asg-instances nat-gw-az-b); do ssh $i sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu; done` — applying.
Eva (netops): MSS clamp applied to nat-gw-az-b pool at 1880123602. monitoring.
Alice (oncall): monitoring dashboards: p95 back to normal in 4m, p99 trending down, stalls dropping from 23% to 6%.
Carmen (sre): collecting packet captures for postmortem; saving `pcap_euw_ez_b_18801236.pcap` and logs: TLS handshake timeouts spiked at 1880123300-1880123450 consistent with the config push.
Ben (infra): rolling revert of egress LB change in AZ-b started at 1880123660 to fully remove the config diff that likely reduced MTU.
Diego (support): contacted top customers again with update that we implemented a mitigation and are routing traffic; Ask if they'd like traffic pinned to AZ-d for now.
Acme reply (via Diego): "we're seeing recovery. please keep us posted, thanks."
Alice (oncall): status page: update to "mitigation in progress, majority of streaming traffic restored; continued monitoring". Assigning postmortem owners: Carmen (sre) + Ben (infra) + Eva (netops).
Carmen (sre): postmortem action items (initial): 1) block rollouts that change egress MTU without canary checks 2) add automated MTU sanity check to predeploy CI 3) ensure NAT pool health exposes MSS drop counters to alerts 4) run game-day for cross-AZ egress path failovers.
Ben (infra): I'll follow up on permanent routing changes and consider per-AZ dedicated NAT pools to avoid noisy neighbour effects.
Eva (netops): will add MSS clamp as a temporary default for affected paths until upstream fix is validated. also will coordinate with network provider for MTU consistency.
Alice (oncall): summary for the incident timeline to include: detection (1880123456), canary failover (1880123502), MSS clamp applied (1880123602), partial revert started (1880123660), containment (1880123720), monitoring stable (1880123820). I'll close paging after final confirmation.
Diego (support): customers updated, no reported regression. closing temporary notifications.
Incident Bot: Incident marked 'mitigated' by Alice (oncall) at 1880123820. Please file incident report and postmortem doc in #postmortems with links to pcaps and deploy diffs.
Alice (oncall): thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and tag owners. If anything else pops up, re-page me.
Ben (infra): noted, will add config diff and rollback logs to the doc.
Carmen (sre): saving all captures and metrics dashboards to the incident folder. preliminary severity: Sev2 (service degradation for multiple customers, partial SLO breach briefly).
Eva (netops): will coordinate follow-up with provider. thanks all. :thumbsup:
